subject: Renewal structure: tethered burst windows + annualization options
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom@stellardata.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stellardata.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — renewal structure and burst capacity options

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting our renewal committee aligned and want to discuss alternatives to the straight annual renewal you proposed. A few priorities from our side:

- Multi-year visibility (2–3 years) but with predictable mid-term scale-ups if Q3 usage exceeds forecasts
- Ability to co-term multiple Redwood products (inference + observability) on a single billing schedule
- An option to opt-out of auto-renew if we hit a business case re-evaluation

Would Redwood be open to a structure that:
1) locks in list pricing for 24 months,
2) has two pre-defined mid-term "burst windows" where we can temporarily add capacity at a capped overage rate, and
3) allows one annualization toggle to switch from quarterly billing to annual invoicing mid-contract?

Happy to share a redline — attaching an internal outline of our ask. Can you loop in someone on pricing / procurement?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, StellarData
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom@stellardata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — renewal structure and burst capacity options

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity. All of your asks are reasonable and we have a few levers that could map cleanly. Quick notes before we formalize:

- Multi-year price lock: we can do 24 or 36 months with an escalator clause tied to usage tiers rather than a blanket CPI increase.
- Burst windows: we offer two predefined burst windows per 12-month period (30-day max each). We can cap burst unit pricing at +40% over baseline committed unit cost.
- Co-terming: we can align product SKUs to a single invoice; co-terming will require a short pro-rata alignment at signature.
- Auto-renew opt-out: we can add a 60-day notice opt-out for enterprise contracts instead of automatic renewal.

I'll attach a draft renewal term sheet and a sample SOW for a staged-burst credit table. Rishi, Priyom — can you review the burst pricing and confirm whether a +40% cap is feasible for StellarData's expected Q3 profile? If not, what's the minimum cap we can offer and any constraints on the number of burst activations?

Tom — can you send the internal forecast ranges (baseline / expected peak) for Q3 so we can model economics?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — renewal structure and burst capacity options

Marissa —

Reviewed the baseline assumptions. A few technical constraints and commercial options:

- Burst pricing: +40% cap is OK on N1-equivalent GPU pools up to 2x baseline for the 30-day window, provided we reserve a soft-gate for capacity in the region (us-west). Beyond 2x we need a different pricing ladder.
- Mid-term scale mechanics: prefer "tethered" increments (commit increases that carry forward rather than true one-off overage). Tethered increases avoid re-underwriting and keep unit economics simple.

Commercial proposal we can present:
A) 24-month term, baseline commit X, two 30-day burst windows at up to 2x baseline at +40% unit price, tethered increase option once per 12 months that annualizes into next year commit at agreed uplift.
B) Co-terming: we perform a one-time pro-rata invoice to align other Redwood SKUs to the 24-month boundary at signature.

Priyom — can you draft an SOW table with the tethered increment math and a sample invoice pro-forma for pro-rata? I'll validate capacity gating with infra ops.

Rishi
Head of Dedicated Accounts
From: Tom Ellis <tom@stellardata.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stellardata.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — renewal structure and burst capacity options

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We like option A but have two asks before we sign: 

1) Can we get one onboarding credit (applied in month 1) to offset migration testing?
2) If we exercise a tethered increase in the first 12 months, can the annualization into year 2 be smoothed across the remaining months (i.e., a linearized uplift) rather than frontloading?

I'll attach a short procurement checklist. If you can queue a doc with those two items included, Procurement can fast-track through approvals.

Tom

Attachments: StellarData_internal_requirements.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom@stellardata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — renewal structure and burst capacity options

Tom —

Great — we've updated the draft to reflect the two items: onboarding credit (one-time credit equal to 10% of month-1 committed spend) and a linearized annualization for any tethered increases exercised in the first 12 months (spread evenly across remaining months of year 2).

Key points in the attached Renewal_Draft_v2: 
- 24-month term with a price lock and a usage escalator tied to tier thresholds (not CPI).
- Two 30-day burst windows per 12 months, up to 2x baseline, capped at +40% unit price.
- Tethered increase mechanism: one election per 12 months; if elected in year 1, the uplift is linearized into year 2 across the remaining months.
- Co-terming: pro-rata invoice to align Redwood Observability license to the 24-month boundary; Cleans up on signature.
- Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out notice (enterprise).

Rishi / Priyom — please confirm capacity gating (us-west soft-gate) and add the SOW table with exact unit math to the SOW_burst_credit_table.xlsx. Neha — pinging you to start a quick contract review on the linearized annualization clause (and to confirm whether legal needs an alternate waterfall if StellarData scales >3x).

Tom — if Procurement signs off we can turn this into a DocuSign package within 48 hours.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: StellarData_Renewal_Draft_v2.pdf; SOW_burst_credit_table.xlsx
